Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead said about it: The Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) rule I take is that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the centre of gravity, meaning centre of gravity (CG, meaning balance point of the machine), so a raised heavy load can tip the machine, and the dump clearance simulation (E51) puts the hopper pivot at 0.550 m over a 0.400 m bin lip for 0.150 m clearance shown in the side view rear dump sketch (E53).
Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead said about it: I take from the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) the rule that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the Centre of Gravity (CG, meaning balance point of the machine), to mean from blind-operation view that the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU, meaning motion sensor for tilt and turn) tilt check must gate the tilt command and trips stay at 15.0 kg with 0.150 m lip clearance from the tip dump clearance deployed vs stowed and pressure check simulation (E51).
Power Structure and Integration Lead said about it: I take the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) rule that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the Centre of Gravity (CG, meaning balance point of the machine) to mean the rear pivot lugs, tilt motor and power bus must be sized for 15.0 kg soil plus steel at 0.550 m pivot clearing the 0.400 m lip from the tip dump clearance check (E51), so Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead please keep 15.0 kg trips and Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead please keep the level-only dump gate.
Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead said about it: I take from the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) the rule that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the balance point, so I confirm trips stay at 15.0 kg dumped only on level ground for safety factor 1.69; I take from the Single Drum Trench Cutters (E45) the finding that transverse cutters concentrate all power in one drum for tough ground, which from my side means the transverse milling drum loosener (C31) fits traction but must still fit the 16.4 W ladder power from the ladder power estimate (E59), so Power Structure and Integration Lead please keep the fused ladder branch and Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead please keep current-limit backout.
Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead said about it: I take from the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) the rule that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the balance point, which for blind operation means the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU, meaning tilt and turn sensor) level check gates the tilt command; pivot 0.550 m clears the 0.400 m lip by 0.150 m with factor 1.69 level-only at 15.0 kg trips from the tip dump clearance check (E51), like a wheelbarrow held flat, so dumping only when level keeps it upright.
Power Structure and Integration Lead said about it: I take from the Systems, devices, and/or methods regarding excavating (E57) and its patent twin (E56) the finding that an excavator backs crowd motion off on detected hoist-motor stall, which for this device means the ladder driver must be a current-limited fused branch that folds back before the fuse blows; I take from the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) the rule that a raised load transfers weight and raises the Centre of Gravity (CG, meaning balance point), which for this device means the rear pivot lugs plus tilt motor carry 15.0 kg soil plus steel at 0.550 m pivot clearing the 0.400 m lip from the tip dump clearance check (E51).
Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead said about it: I take from the Systems, devices, and/or methods regarding excavating (E57) and its twin CA2784416C patent (E56) the finding that crowd backs off on hoist stall, which for my ladder plus screw means current-limit foldback plus 0.600 s reverse from the tag align and backout simulation (E58) protects the 16.4 W ladder power from the ladder power estimate (E59); pivot 0.550 m clears 0.400 m lip by 0.150 m from the tip dump clearance check (E51) with align 0.030 to 0.040 m, finger width against 0.150 m mouth, and level-only 15 kg trips hold factor 1.69 per the Skid-Steer Safety rule (E47).
